## What you just did, as diagrams
:::

```{=html}
<div id="k8-explain" class="lx-xgrid">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<dl class="lx-ideas">
<dt>Commit</dt><dd>The unit of <span class="lx-term" data-term="version-control">version control</span>: a saved snapshot of every file, with a message, a parent and an id; git add picks what goes in, git commit records it.</dd>
<dt>Three places</dt><dd>A change sits in the working folder, then the staging area, then the history.</dd>
<dt>Branch</dt><dd>A movable label on a line of commits: a what-if lives on its own branch while main stays as it was.</dd>
<dt>Halving the history</dt><dd>With one good and one bad commit, check the middle each time: 1,000 commits need at most 10 checks.</dd>
<dt><span class="lx-term" data-term="hidden-state">Hidden state</span></dt><dd>A notebook's memory can be older than its code; only Restart and run all shows the outputs come from the cells as written.</dd>
<dt>Clean rerun</dt><dd>A fresh clone and a pinned install give the same numbers: the code and inputs reproduce the result, which is not the same as the result being right.</dd>
</dl>
</div>
</div>
```

```{=html}
<div class="lx-deepers">
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Analyst</span>What a commit stores, and why its id changes</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **A snapshot, not a list of edits.** A commit stores every file as it was, plus the author, the time, the message and its parent's id. Files that did not change are shared with the parent, not copied.
- **The id is a fingerprint.** Git computes it with SHA-1 over all of that (a SHA-256 format also exists). Change one byte, the message or the parent, and the id changes.
- **Branches are labels.** `main` and `high-gas` each point at one commit; a new commit moves the current label forward. Creating a branch copies no files.
- **Merging.** `git merge high-gas` [joins]{.lx-term term="merge"} two lines of work. If main has not moved, its label just moves forward (a fast-forward). If both changed, Git combines them line by line and stops with a conflict where both edited the same lines (this page's model compares whole files).

```{=html}
</div>
</details>
<details class="lx-deeper">
<summary><span class="k">Go deeper · Modeler</span>Make reruns automatic</summary>
<div class="lx-deeper-body">
```

- **Tests that run themselves.** Keep the asserts (the balance, totals, a known case) in test files and run them on every commit, on your computer or on a hosted service that runs them for each push.
- **Notebooks without hidden state.** Execute them from a fresh kernel without a browser (`jupyter nbconvert --to notebook --execute day.ipynb`), or keep the model in `.py` files and let the notebook call and plot.
- **Exact environments.** A lock file records the exact version of every package, including the ones your packages depend on.
- **Tag the result.** `git tag v1.0` marks the commit behind a published number, so anyone can return to it.
- **Where next:** [M1](m01-dispatch-to-lmp.html)'s notebook asserts the browser's prices; R5 (upcoming) puts a whole model through planted bugs, a benchmark and a clean-clone rerun.

```{=html}

</div>
```

## Check yourself
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="k8-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="save" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “Saving a file in the editor records it in Git's history.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Saving changes the working folder only; git add and then git commit record a snapshot.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="cells" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If every cell of a notebook ran without an error, its outputs match the code on the page.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. On this page cell 4 showed 78600 under a cell that says 55, with no error; only Restart and run all shows the outputs come from the cells as written.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="clone" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If a fresh clone reruns and gives the same numbers, the model's answer is right.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. Commit 4's sign error reran just as cleanly and gave 4,787 MWh every time; a check such as the balance assert is what catches an error like that.</p></details>
</div>
</div>

<div class="lx-quiz" data-quiz="k8">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="twice" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">You edit model.py, run git add model.py, then edit model.py again. What does git commit record?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">Both edits</li><li data-value="b">Only the first edit</li><li data-value="c">Only the second edit</li><li data-value="d">Nothing</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Only the first edit: git add staged that version. The second edit waits in the working folder until you add it too.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="halve" data-answer="b">
<p class="lx-qtext">Commit 1 of 9 passes the balance check and commit 9 fails it. Checking the middle each time, at most how many commits must you check?</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="a">2</li><li data-value="b">3</li><li data-value="c">4</li><li data-value="d">8</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>3: eight suspects (commits 2 to 9), halved three times, leave one. Checking one by one can take 7.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div id="k8-drill">
<div class="lx-card k8-drill"><div class="lx-x-head"><h3>Practice drill</h3></div>
<p class="lx-hint">With JavaScript on, a drill of seven kinds of item, about two minutes each (fifteen items take about 30 minutes). Three worked items:</p>
<!-- k8-drill:start (written by _tests/learn/test_k08-git-notebooks.js in its write mode; do not edit) -->
<ol class="k8-static-drill">
<li>A commit's diff shows “- gas_cost: 40” and “+ gas_cost: 30” in params.yml. The model makes 1,965 MWh of gas. What is the day's gas cost after this commit, in $? <b>Answer: $58,950.</b> 1,965 MWh × $30/MWh = $58,950 (it was $78,600).</li>
<li>Commit 1 of 64 passes the check; commit 64 fails it. Checking the middle commit each time, at most how many commits must you check to find the first bad one? <b>Answer: 6.</b> 63 suspects; each check halves them: 2^6 = 64 ≥ 63 &gt; 2^5 = 32, so 6 checks.</li>
<li>Fresh kernel. Cells: (1) load the day, (2) gas_cost = 40, (3) gas_mwh = … (1,965), (4) gas_mwh * gas_cost. You: run cell 3, run cell 1, run cell 2, run cell 4. What does cell 4 show? <b>Answer: an error: a name is not defined.</b> NameError: name 'gas_mwh' is not defined: a cell it needs has not run yet.</li>
</ol>
<!-- k8-drill:end -->
</div>
</div>
```

## Commands, sources and what's next
:::

::: {.lx-end}
```{=html}
<div class="lx-card">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Commands to remember</p>
<div class="lx-scroll-x">
<table class="lx-facts k8-cmdtab">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Command</th><th scope="col">What it does</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><td class="n">git status</td><td>Lists staged, edited and new files.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git diff</td><td>Shows edited lines not yet staged; git diff &lt;id&gt; &lt;id&gt; compares two commits.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git add &lt;file&gt;</td><td>Stages a file's current version for the next commit.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git commit -m "why"</td><td>Records the staged snapshot with a message.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git log --oneline</td><td>The history, one commit per line, newest first.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git switch -c &lt;name&gt;</td><td>Starts a branch here; git switch &lt;name&gt; moves between branches.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git restore &lt;file&gt;</td><td>Throws away a file's edits since it was last staged.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git revert &lt;id&gt;</td><td>Adds a commit that undoes an earlier one.</td></tr>
<tr><td class="n">git clone &lt;source&gt;</td><td>Makes a fresh copy of a project with its whole history.</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
```
